answer: In this PoA design, identity verification uses a VDF: each challenge requires a prescribed chain of dependent modular squarings, while a Wesolowski proof certifies the result. An attacker simulating multiple clones cannot split any chain across GPUs; every clone must endure its own sequential delay. Thus identities named pearl, sparrow, or jetty cannot be multiplied cheaply, because the physical time bottleneck remains unavoidable.
